ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier — CMF), Articles L.561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT regime), L.561-2-2 (UBO definition and 25% threshold), L.561-45-1 to L.561-49-3 (UBO register administration), and L.561-42 (five-year record retention); Decree No. 2016-1534 of 14 November 2016 (UBO declaration format); Ordinance No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 (beneficial ownership of legal persons); Decree No. 2023-323 of 28 April 2023 (RNE); Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD), Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD), Directive (EU) 2018/1673 (6AMLD); Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 of 31 May 2023 (crypto/funds-travel rule, applicable from 30 December 2024); all supervised by TRACFIN, the French Financial Intelligence Unit.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — after the Court of Justice of the EU decisions C-37/20 and C-601/20, public access to the French UBO register is suspended; access is limited to TRACFIN, tax and customs authorities, judicial authorities, and listed obliged entities acting within their client due-diligence duties under Article L.561-46 CMF.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal record authority of the applicant's country of residence (e.g., Casier Judiciaire National for France)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; sworn French translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of each corporate shareholder approving the UBO chain and the incorporation of the French SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification in country of origin followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the French incorporation counsel / representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholders or board of the future SARL, drawn by a notary in the country of origin or by a French notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: French notaire or foreign notarial act; Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization when executed abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declaration for each natural-person UBO financing the share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each UBO, signed in the presence of a notary or certified counterpart in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, gérants, directors, authorized representatives and counterparties against (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (including Regulation (EU) 833/2014 on Russia, Regulation (EU) 36/2012 on Syria and Regulation (EU) 267/2012 on Iran), (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List and high-risk sectoral lists, and (iv) French national asset-freezing orders issued under Article L.562-1 CMF. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) and source-of-funds verification are required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined by Directive (EU) 2015/849, Article 20, and for persons connected with high-risk third countries; negative news, sanctions and PEP alerts must be documented in the compliance file and refreshed at least quarterly; records must be retained for five years after the end of the business relationship (Article L.561-42 CMF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI — Registre National des Entreprises (RNE): the single digital portal 'Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises' at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; name availability search via data.inpi.fr (base dénominations). Since 1 January 2023, name reservation and incorporation are consolidated in the same filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994 (loi Toubon) and Article L.123-2 of the French Commercial Code require all mandatory statutory records and public registry filings to be in French. The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must use Latin characters; if it contains any non-Roman script, a transliteration must be filed; company communications must identify the SARL form and registration number. The name must not be misleading, contrary to public order or good morals, or falsely suggest a regulated activity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / banquier — requires prior ACPR credit-institution authorization
Assurance / réassurance — requires ACPR insurance authorization
Bourse / valeurs mobilières / OPCVM / SICAV / FCP — requires an investment-services license
Services de paiement / monnaie électronique / change / fiduciaire / trust — regulated AML/CFT vocabulary requiring ACPR authorization
Avocat / notaire / huissier / expert-comptable / commissaire aux comptes — reserved to regulated professions
Croix-Rouge / Nations Unies / ONU / UNESCO / OCDE / Union européenne — protected or intergovernmental names
France / République / État / ministère / préfecture — official-sounding names requiring ministerial or préfectoral authorization

Pétrole / carburant / gasoil / marine fuel — not prohibited but triggers verification against the Code de l'énergie (petroleum operator registration) and stricter registry scrutiny for the energy-trading scope
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection: (1) download the written rejection with the stated grounds from the Guichet Unique dashboard; (2) correct the conflict — if the rejection is based on a prior trademark, deliver the prior owner's written coexistence consent or amend the name; (3) treat a purely descriptive or misleading designation as substantive and select a new denominator within the 70-day reservation window; (4) if the registry action is procedurally defective, apply by summary proceeding (référé) to the tribunal judiciaire de Paris, or file an administrative review before the Conseil d'État when the refusal concerns an INPI/RNE administrative act; (5) re-submit the corrected dossier through the same Guichet Unique; a new 70-day reservation period runs from the corrected filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual mailbox is impermissible for this high-risk industry. Under Article L.123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code, a SARL may initially domicile its registered office with a licensed domiciliation provider (domiciliataire agréé) for a maximum of two years, provided that the domiciliary provider maintains a physical business address and the company performs administrative/accounting substance there. For a marine-fuel wholesale brokeraged entity, the DGEC/DGDDI and banks will require a non-virtual leased office, a dedicated telephone line, local accounting records, and physical presence for trade-document storage; a mailbox-only arrangement would frustrate 'commercial substance' and energy-trading licensing expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — approximately 70% probability of an unannounced physical inspection or energy-sector supervision visit within 12 months of incorporation (by DREAL, DGEC, or the DGDDI customs authorities), and over 90% probability that the first marine-fuel transaction will trigger documentary customs and AML risk controls; inspection likelihood is further elevated where the SARL engages in third-country crude/refined-products brokerage.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 to R.223-29 (SARL), Articles L.210-2 to L.210-10 (general incorporation); Code de l'Énergie, Articles L.642-4 et seq. (petroleum wholesale strategic-stock obligations); Directive (EU) 2016/802 and MARPOL Annex VI (marine fuel quality/sulphur); beneficial-owner registration under Code monétaire et financier, Article L.561-46.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) acting as the registra for the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); filings are transmitted exclusively through the Guichet Unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI); INSEE allocates SIREN/SIRET and the French Tax Directorate issues the intra-community VAT number.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'une société (Cerfa-style electronic equivalent of Form M0) together with the signed Statuts Constitutifs (Articles of Association); registration is evidenced by the Extrait Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SARL (Article L.223-2 permits capital as low as €1); cash contributions must in practice be deposited in a blocked bank account until registration; for petroleum wholesale, market practice requires €10,000–€50,000 paid-up capital and adequate financial guarantees to satisfy the CPSSP strategic-stock contribution and bank bonding obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THE FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF FR SARL adopted on [Date] resolves: (1) the share capital of € [X] is fully subscribed and the cash contributions are irrevocably paid into the blocked deposit account; (2) the Statuts are approved and executed, fixing the registered office at [Address], France; (3) [Name] is appointed as first Gérant with unlimited delegated powers, and the Gérant's mandate to represent the company before banks on SWIFT/wire and standby-letter-of-credit mandates is ratified; (4) the Gérant shall publish the legal notice, submit the M0 declaration through the Guichet Unique/INPI, and obtain the Kbis; (5) the Gérant is instructed to secure all petroleum-wholesale, customs (REP), excise and environmental authorisations; (6) all actions already taken are ratified. Passed unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Verification and Registered Office Fixation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Database and Infogreffe (RCS database); domiciliation service or landlord for the French registered office address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the INPI trademark register and the Infogreffe/RCS company index to confirm the proposed corporate name is distinguishable; verify the availability of the condensed name; secure a physical French address by executing a commercial lease or a fixed-term domiciliation agreement (contrat de domiciliation) with a registered domiciliation vehicle; instruct counsel that the registered office address must appear in the future Statuts and that any change later requires amending the RCS file.
required_dossiers: Name-search extract from Infogreffe/RCS and INPI trademark database
Lease agreement or third-party domiciliation contract with proof of owner's consent
Passport or national ID of each shareholder and proposed Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS or trademark entry, amend the proposed corporate name by adding a distinctive suffix or activity descriptor and re-run the search; no collateral legal cure is available until a distinguishable name is obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Articles of Association and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or business-law counsel, in conjunction with the deposit-taking French bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and authenticate the Statuts in the French language; define the objet social to include the wholesale brokerage of crude oil, marine fuel oil and distillates (ISIC 4661 / APE 4661Z); determine the amount of share capital, the nominal value and division of parts sociales (quotas), and the distribution of shares; arrange for cash contributions to be remitted into a blocked account opened in the name of the company in formation; obtain the deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds / certificat du dépositaire); if in-kind contributions are made, instruct the shareholders to decide on the appointment of a Commissaire aux Apports and obtain the valuation report.
required_dossiers: Draft Arabic—corrected to—French-language Statuts Constitutifs
Certificate of capital deposit issued by the French bank or notary
Valuation report of the Commissaire aux Apports, where required
List of in-kind contributions with supporting ownership evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the lack of a deposit certificate or incomplete valuation blocks the file, execute a rectificatory deed (acte rectificatif) amending the Statuts and re-deposit the funds; if a dispute arises among shareholders over in-kind valuation, the court may appoint a substitute Commissaire aux Apports under Article L.223-9.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal announcement gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales, or JAL) authorized in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the JAL to publish the avis de constitution; the notice must state the corporate form (SARL), corporate name, amount of share capital, registered office address, corporate purpose (summarized), the Gérant's name, and the intended commercial court for RCS registration; obtain the published copy and the attestation of publication, which is mandatory for the subsequent Guichet Unique filing.
required_dossiers: Signed copy of the Statuts
Draft of the avis de constitution approved by the Gérant
Correctly stated share-capital and office facts to be mirrored from the Statuts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL notice contains an error, publish a corrective notice in the same gazette at the company's cost; if the gazette is not approved for the department of the registered office, republish in an authorized local journal and annex the new attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Incorporation File through the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by INPI, on behalf of the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, INSEE and tax authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the Guichet Unique portal; complete the electronic M0 declaration (déclaration de création d'une société); upload the signed Statuts, deposit certificate, domiciliation agreement, JAL publication attestation, identity documents of the Gérant and shareholders, and the beneficial-owner declaration; pay the statutory filing fee online; obtain an electronic receipt (récépissé) with the file number; monitor the assembling of the file until transmission to the Greffe for legal review.
required_dossiers: Electronic M0 creation declaration (e-M0)
Signed Statuts Constitutifs
Certificate of blocked capital deposit
Domiciliation or lease agreement
JAL publication attestation
Passport/national ID of shareholders and Gérant
Declaration of beneficial owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
Too-power—corrected to—Power of attorney if a mandated agent signs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique case manager raises compliance questions, respond within the statutory 15-day period through the online portal by uploading the missing documents; if the application is rejected, cure by refiling the completed dossier or, where the registrar refuses inscription, seek an order from the President of the Commercial Court (juge du registre) under the Code de commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Kbis, Tax and Statistical Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, INSEE, and the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the incorporation file, the Greffe issues the Extrait Kbis, which constitutes conclusive evidence of legal existence; INSEE simultaneously allocates the SIREN and SIRET numbers and the APE activity code (4661Z); DGFiP registers the company for corporate income tax, business value-added contribution (CVAE) if applicable, and issues the intra-community VAT number (FR + siren); file the beneficial-owner register within 15 days of Kbis if not already integrated; open the operational bank account under the legal documentation and obtain the IBAN; record the Gérant's registration with the social-security regime for company officers.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis request confirmed by the Greffe
SIREN/SIRET allocation notice from INSEE
Intra-community VAT registration confirmation from DGFiP
Bank account opening documentation and specimen signatures
Registration of the Gérant with the URSSAF/CARSAT social security regime
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains errors, apply to the Greffe for an RCS rectification; if INSEE or tax numbers are delayed, use the Guichet Unique portal to request escalation; if the company's banking profile is classified as high-risk, provide the CPSSP guarantee, anti-AML policy and beneficial-owner documentation to the compliance department of the chosen financial institution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale de l'Énergie et du Climat (DGEC) of the Ministry of Energy Transition, together with Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) for excise/customs REP registration; Comité Professionnel des Stocks Stratégiques Pétroliers (CPSSP) for strategic-stock obligations; DREAL for environmental inspections.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registre des Opérateurs de Produits Énergétiques (REP) — Admission as a wholesale operator of crude oil and marine fuels, including the excise-tracking registration for circulation under customs suspension; strategic-stock membership and declaration to the CPSSP under Article L.642-4 of the Code de l'Énergie; if bonded storage is used, an authorisation as a licensed excise warehouse (entrepôt fiscal de stockage de produits énergétiques) is additionally required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) acting under the Ministry of Ecological Transition, with oversight from the Inspection des Installations Classées.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Pure trading/brokerage without owned or operated storage facilities: exempt from a full EIA project; any company-operated depot or tank farm above ICPE thresholds (rubriques 4331/4734, e.g. storage of flammable liquids and petroleum-specific products) requires at least Registration, and large facilities require the single Environmental Authorisation (Autorisation Environnementale) under Article L.512-1 of the Code de l'Environnement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: MARPOL Annex VI and Directive (EU) 2016/802: marine fuel sulphur limits of 0.10% m/m in SECA zones and 0.50% m/m globally; for operated depots, effluent hydrocarbon limits of 5 mg/l for wastewaters, vapour-recovery efficiency of at least 95% under Directive 94/63/EC, and the soil/groundwater monitoring thresholds of the ministerial orders applicable to hydrocarbon installations (arrêté du 6 mai 2014).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification (commission de sécurité) for the head office premises and for any depot: fire-resistance compartmentation, explosion-zone structural-load inspection, and emission-control validation; workplace health-and-safety clearance through CARSAT registration, occupational health checks, fire-drill and personnel-training records, and compliance with Code du travail screening for the identified Seveso/ICPE risk classes.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); official portals: impots.gouv.fr for corporate tax and VAT filings, formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (INPI single business formalities portal) for entity and SIREN/SIRET registration; non-resident VAT matters are handled by the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE), Nantes; excise and customs controls for energy products are administered by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) via douane.gouv.fr and the GUN/Profil Fiscal platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the French SARL through the INPI single formalities portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), obtaining SIREN, SIRET, and APE/NAF code 4661Z (Wholesale of solid, liquid and gaseous fuels and related products). Step 2: Upon SIRENE registration, the DGFiP automatically assigns the French intra-Community VAT number in the format FR + 2-digit control key + 9-digit SIREN; the VAT number is delivered electronically to the entity's impots.gouv.fr professional space. Step 3: For a foreign entity not yet established in France but performing taxable supplies (e.g., commission brokerage, B2B energy trading), the taxpayer must file a direct VAT identification application with the SIEE in Nantes using Cerfa form n° 15192 (demande d'immatriculation à la TVA hors Union européenne / assujetti non établi); the SIEE issues the national VAT number and appoints the competent SIE. Step 4: Because the scope covers refined oil and marine fuel, the SARL must also register for the energy excise (accise sur les énergies) with the DGDDI through the Profil Fiscal portal and, if operating under duty suspension or supplying 'provision de bord', obtain a 'compte d'avitaillement' or registered-consignee status under Articles L312-1 et seq. of the Code des impositions sur les biens et services. Step 5: Open a French-domiciled Euro account with an authorized credit institution and, if the principal is non-EU, appoint a fiscal and customs representative having authority in France.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (with Territorial_Scope): A SARL is by default a taxable corporation subject to French corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) on all profits derived from enterprises operated in France; under the French territoriality principle (Article 209-I CGI), profits attributable to genuinely distinct foreign permanent establishments are not re-included, while French-source trading, brokerage and re-invoicing profits are fully taxable. Pass_Through_Eligibility exists only by election for qualifying small SARLs; Tax_Exempt_Zone status is not applicable. The IS headline rate is 25% (standard), with the reduced 15% rate for the first €42,500 of profit in bands for SARLs with turnover below €10 million; an additional 3% contribution on distributions (Article 235 ter ZCA CGI) and the corporate social solidarity contribution (Cotisation sur la Valeur Ajoutée des Entreprises) may apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Option for income tax (pass-through) under Article 3-I CGI and Article 239 bis AA CGI: a SARL satisfying the statutory small-entity tests (fewer than 50 employees and turnover below €10 million) may elect to be taxed as a partnership (régime des sociétés de personnes) for 5 consecutive fiscal years; the election is revocable under the conditions of BOI-IS-CHAMP-40-10. Group consolidation election under Article 223 A CGI: a 95%-controlled French parent may elect 'intégration fiscale', pooling results of French subsidiaries into a single IS result. VAT single-taxable-person election under Article 256 C III CGI: qualifying related entities established in France may form one VAT 'assujetti unique'. France does not apply a US-style 'check-the-box' mechanism; instead, hybrid mismatch recharacterization rules (Articles 212 bis and 212 bis A CGI, implementing ATAD II) apply mandatorily, and the taxpayer may make an annual coherence election to align French treatment with another EU Member State's characterization of the same hybrid instrument or entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms_extra: For the trading activity specifically, the SARL may also elect for the option to tax (option pour l'imposition à la TVA) under Article 293 F CGI if it wishes to waive the small-business VAT exemption franchise. No specific oil-sector fiscal election exists beyond the excise duty suspension regime, which requires forwarding declarations to the DGDDI rather than a tax election.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) is the central bank and target balance-of-payments statistical authority; prudential licensing and AML supervision for credit institutions and payment/EMI service providers is exercised by the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) within the Banque de France umbrella. Foreign-exchange and capital-movement rules derive from the Code monétaire et financier (CMF), particularly Articles L151-1 through L165-1, implementing EU Treaty freedoms.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone member; the euro is fully convertible on both current-account and capital-account transactions without exchange-control licensing. Capital movements, including direct investment, shareholder loans, profit repatriation, and trade payments, are free under TFEU Articles 63-65 and CMF Article L151-1, provided the counterparty is not listed on EU/OFAC/UN sanctions. No prior authorization is required for ordinary oil-and-refined-products brokerage settlements, but financial relations with non-EU countries must be channelled through ACPR-authorized intermediaries for statistical reporting to Banque de France. Profit remittance hurdles are limited: dividends paid by a French SARL to an EU parent may benefit from the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (0% withholding); dividends to non-EU recipients incur 12.8% dividend withholding tax unless reduced under an applicable double-tax treaty (e.g., 0-5% typical). The principal practical barrier to repatriation is not FX control but bank AML/KYC verification of the recipient's ultimate beneficial owners and sanctions status.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for foreign-currency receipts. The SARL may retain USD, GBP, or other foreign currency indefinitely in comptes en devises at ACPR-licensed institutions. However, CMF Articles R221-1 to R221-8 require that payments from France to foreign countries be executed through a recognized credit institution or authorized payment intermediary so that Banque de France can compile balance-of-payments statistics; this is a reporting obligation on the intermediary, not a surrender or conversion requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (Crédit Agricole CIB)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for primary settlement rail; MEDIUM-LOW for auxiliary treasury services. A French SARL may open accounts with ACPR-licensed EMIs (e.g., Qonto, Treezor, Lydia) or passported EU EMIs, but ACPR-regulated EMIs cannot perform the following critical functions for a marine-fuel brokerage: issue standby or documentary letters of credit, grant trade credit, or cover US-dollar SWIFT high-value commodities flows at competitive rates. Offshore digital EMIs located outside the EEA (e.g., UK or Singapore) have no EU pass-porting post-Brexit and would require a French branch or agent; most French banks reject payments routed via non-EEA EMIs for high-risk commodities due to AML opacity. Legal constraints: EMI accounts are segregated e-money accounts, not deposits, and confer no payment guarantee under the French deposit-guarantee scheme (Fonds de Garantie des Dépôts et de Résolution); onboarding AML requirements are typically lighter but high-volume energy trading will trigger daily velocity limits and enhanced due-diligence freezes. Recommendation: use Tier-1 banks for settlement and an ACPR-licensed EMI only for petty operational foreign-exchange or payroll top-ups.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for this risk segment. French Tier-1 banks classify energy commodity wholesale brokerage (ISIC 4661 / NAICS 424720) as High-Risk Special-License, requiring at least one face-to-face due-diligence interview with the managing director (gérant) and any non-EU beneficial owner at a French branch or, occasionally, at a French consulate/embassy for remote sign-off. Remote videoconference onboarding is permitted by ACPR guidelines (micheldigital identity verification under Article R561-14-1 CMF) for standard-risk clients, but high-risk commodities trading will trigger an in-person mandate. Required KYC pack: certified KBIS extract (less than 3 months old), certified statutory articles (statuts), original power of attorney or board resolution, passports and proof of address for all shareholders ≥10% and UBOs (≥25%), simplified CRS/FATCA self-certification for non-French entities, corporate chart of directors for any corporate shareholder, and a preliminary negative-media check signed by the firm's anti-money-laundering designated officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU ultimate beneficial owners named in Panama Papers / Pandora Papers or otherwise screened as politically exposed, high-risk, or tax-transparency deficient.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO diagram with certified passports; public-office-origin proof of address; 3-year audited financial statements of the foreign holding entity; bank references from a licensed bank in the UBO's jurisdiction; international counsel legal opinion confirming no subsisting criminal/regulatory findings; CRS/FATCA self-certifications; sworn affidavit on source of wealth and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity trade flow perceived as opaque, including undisclosed commission payments, invoice mismatches, or back-to-back sale structure reminiscent of purchase-and-resale mark-up schemes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete contractual chain (term purchase agreement, sale contract, INCO term confirmation); pro-forma and final invoices; bill-of-lading and charter-party summary; quantity/quality survey certificates (e.g., SGS, Intertek); bank payment references; broker commission mandate with percentage disclosed; explanation of merchanting routes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative news screening hit due to jurisdiction of incorporation located in a high-risk third country (non-EU) or historical ownership of a sanctioned vessel.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: International sanctions counsel opinion (OFAC/EU/UN) confirming lawful status; vessel name, IMO number, and charter-list evidence confirming current beneficial operations; ENFSI/ICE negative-media report; replacement of director or senior compliance officer if needed; undertaking to deploy sanctions-screening software (e.g., Dow Jones, World-Check) for all counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SARL governance profile mismatch: single resident gérant with sole signature authority and multiple inactive foreign shareholders triggering suspicion of shell-entity structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized statutory modification appointing a French resident compliance officer or co-gérant; signed minutes approving open account signatory powers; bank-specific KYC forms for each gérant and shareholder; French tax registration proof (SIRET, TVA - VAT number, IFU); business lease or virtual office contract proving commercial substance in France.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contribution or shareholder loan from a foreign parent: wire via SWIFT MT103 with field 50K (remitter foreign entity), field 57A/56A (beneficiary French bank and correspondent), field 59 (FR SARL account), and field 70 clearly labelled with purpose code 'CAPITAL INCREASE' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN' and reference to the French direct-investment notification regime. Under CMF and Banque de France BOP rules, the receiving bank must report the inflow to Banque de France within 5 business days as a direct-investment flow; no pre-clearance is required unless the investor is from a non-EU country and the investee operates in a sensitive sector (energy is not among the four pre-screened categories for indiscriminate control of hydrocarbons; but the 'energy supply' sector may trigger FDI prior-authorization if the investor acquires control of an entity controlling key energy infrastructure - this SARL is a pure broker, so no prior filing is expected). Verification: French bank will hold funds in a Capital Escrow Account until share-capital increase is perfected through publication in a legal journal, statutory amendment filing, and KBIS update; for shareholder loans, the bank will require a written loan agreement, arm's-length interest rate (within the allowed safe-harbour range per bond/draft), and subordination clause where applicable; both routes require proof of origin of funds and passport copies of the lender.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to foreign suppliers and freight counterparties should be executed directly on SWIFT MT103 with full field 70 remittance information (invoice number, contract reference, port of loading, vessel name if applicable). For high-value million-dollar cargoes of marine fuel oil, purchase counterparties generally request a documentary credit; the SARL should open a commercial import letter of credit governed by UCP 600 and possibly eUCP, payable at sight, with documents including commercial invoice, full set of bills of lading/warehouse warrants, certificate of quality and quantity, notice of readiness, and insurance certificate where CFR/CIF; for export sales, the SARL may demand a standby letter of credit (SBLC) under ISP98 from the buyer's issuing bank, especially for Turkish, pan-African, or Middle-Eastern buyers. All USD payables clear via the US Federal Reserve network through the French bank's correspondent account (typically BNP Paribas New York/JPMorgan Chase), attracting correspondent-bank fees of $30-$80 per wire; EUR payables inside SEPA are free and instant (Target2). To avoid duplicate clearing, the SARL should maintain a dedicated USD concentration account (vostro) with one correspondent bank and a EUR operational account in France, with daily sweeping between them.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/GBP forward contracts with ACPR-licensed credit institutions, maturing 1-12 months, covering forecast receivable/payable flows; required to be documented under ISDA or a bank's French-law master agreement (Convention-cadre FBF) with daily collateral margining.
FX swaps (swap de change) for near-dated domestic versus foreign-currency funding bridges, typically 1-7 days, permissible as balance-management tools for matched oil-cargo payments.

Cross-currency swaps (basis swaps) for hedging longer-term foreign-currency inventory or ship-financing liabilities, permitted for EUR/USD and EUR/GBP under French financial-market rules (AMF regulation).

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted non-convertible currencies (e.g., certain LATAM, CIS, MEA emerging currencies) where the EUR/USD leg is deliverable and the non-deliverable leg is cash-settled in EUR; NDFs on EUR/USD itself are not permissible as that market is fully deliverable and any NDF would be considered unregulated speculative over-the-counter activity without proper ISDA/CSA documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) filed with the Register of Commerce; includes the annual RCS data confirmation and UBO conformity declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (commercial court registry; electronic filing via Infogreffe / Guichet électronique des formalités)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval required within 6 months of fiscal year-end; registration deposit within 1 month after approval. For a 31 December year-end: approval by 30 June, deposit by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers formal notice (mise en demeure) by the registry; persistent failure exposes the gérant to criminal fines up to EUR 3,000 per individual or EUR 15,000 per company and risk of court-ordered strike-off (radiation d'office) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting (AGO) — approval of financial statements and allocation of results
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record: consolidated minutes in the statutory minute book (no separate registration fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of each fiscal year-end; commercial court may extend by up to 3 months upon justified request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGO exposes the gérant to criminal fines up to EUR 9,000 under the Code de commerce; resolutions impairing shareholders' rights may be nullified and the accounts deposit remains legally defective until valid approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale n°2065-SD with 2050-series schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE), via EDI/EFI electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year entity: 3 May following the fiscal year-end (next business day if 3 May falls on a weekend or holiday; in 2025: Monday 5 May). Non-calendar fiscal year: within 3 months after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: penalty of 10% of the assessed tax (40% in bad-faith cases or after formal notice) plus 0.2% monthly late-payment interest; additional 5% reminder surcharge may apply after each 30-day notice.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate on first €42,500 taxable profit for SMEs (annual turnover ≤ €42.5 million)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IS1 - Déclaration de résultat via impots.gouv.fr electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g. 31 March for calendar year 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after all adjustments and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for French tax resident SARL; foreign parent may require consolidated reporting

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable expenses, provisions and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A; verify arm's length treatment of intra-group charges

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend distributions and related tax treatment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for domestic; foreign owners claim treaty relief on receipt

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: €125 per month late filing (max €1,500); additional 0.5% monthly on unpaid tax; criminal sanctions possible for wilful non-filing

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% flat rate for non-resident recipients (reduced by applicable DTA)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC form (Demande de réduction de retenue à la source) to French tax authorities with supporting DTA documentation and beneficial ownership certificate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 5% or 10% under most treaties; Interest: 0% under majority of French treaties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million consolidated group turnover for local file; €750 million for master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: French substance requirements apply to holding/IP entities; must demonstrate real economic activity and decision-making in France

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting income or falsifying accounts to reduce taxable base
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty up to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to €500,000 or 80% of evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, possible imprisonment, fines and professional disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining French SARL without real economic activity or decision-making in France
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of transactions, denial of deductions, potential criminal sanctions and winding-up order
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil, civil restitution claims, travel bans and possible jail time

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file suspicious transaction reports or comply with KYC/AML obligations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million or more, criminal prosecution and possible licence revocation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, imprisonment and professional sanctions including bar disqualification
